STATE OF MAINE 
PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION

ANDRO HYDRO, LLC 
Request for Approval of Certification 
For RPS Eligibility (Otis Unit #1 Facility) 

Procedural Order (Requesting 
Additional Information) 

On January 12, 2026, Andro Hydro LLC (Andro Hydro) requested certification 
of a 5.175 megawatt (MW) alternating current (AC) hydroelectric facility located in 
Livermore Falls, ME (the facility) as a Class I and Class IA renewable resource eligible 
to satisfy Maine’s new renewable resource portfolio (or renewable portfolio standard 
(RPS)) requirement pursuant to Chapter 311 of the Commission’s rules. On July 10, 
2026, Andro Hydro filed supplemental information in the docket. 
Andro Hydro’s Statement Regarding Operation Viability of Otis Unit 1 
(Statement) provides information about the project based on Andro Hydro’s review of 
inspection records, field reports, vendor communications and photographic 
documentation. Section 2.1 of the Statement refers to two reports, cited as: 
• Cianbros Wicket Gate Clearance Report; and 
• Cianbros Recommendations for Wicket Gates. 

Section 3.4 of the Statement refers to a series of daily reports, cited as: 
• Hydro Tech Inc. Technical Oversight Daily Reports, Days 1-12, August-
October 2025; 
• Daily Report Day 2, August 8, 2025; and 
• Daily Report, Day 5, October 1, 2025. 

The Commission would like to review the reports cited in Andro Hydro’s 
Statement. To the extent any of these reports contain confidential information, Andro 
Hydro is invited to submit a redacted version of these reports along with a request for 
a protective order explaining why certain information contained in the reports must be 
protected. 
Dated at Hallowell, Maine, this 13th day of July, 2026.

Presiding Officer

PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION 

PROCEDURAL ORDER 
Inquiry into Flexible Interconnection 
(Scheduling Workshop) 

On August 4, 2026, the Commission will hold a workshop to discuss the status of 
flexible interconnection opportunities and the challenges posed to developing more 
opportunities. The workshop will be limited to existing efforts to develop flexible 
interconnection and barriers to implementing the technology. 

Both Investor Owned Utilities will provide presentations at the workshop. There 
may be an opportunity for other interested persons to present. Interested persons 
should reach out to Presiding Officer to discuss their proposed presentation and to see 
if the agenda will allow for the opportunity.

Participation will also be available through Microsoft Teams. Persons interested in 
participating remotely may email the Presiding Officer to request the Teams link or the 
dial-in information.

title: 2026-07-09 Order Granting Waiver 2026-00178.pdf
text:
STATE OF MAINE 
PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION 

Docket No. 2026-00178 

July 9, 2026 

MONSON UTILITIES DISTRICT 
Request for Approval of Rate Change 
Pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 6104 

ORDER GRANTING WAIVER 

BARTLETT, Chair; SCULLY and GILBERT, Commissioners 
I. 
SUMMARY 
By this Order, the Director of Telephone and Water Utility Industries grants a 
waiver of the auditing requirements of Chapter 710 of the Commission’s Rules, thereby 
permitting the Monson Utilities District (the District) to file a rate increase pursuant to 35-
A M.R.S. § 6104 without audited financial statements.1 
II. 
PROCEDURAL BACKGROUND 
On June 30, 2026, the District filed information supporting a proposed rate 
increase pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 6104 with the Commission. 
The District also requested a waiver of Chapter 710 of the Commission’s Rules, 
which requires consumer owned water utilities have an audit made of its accounts by a 
qualified independent certified public accountant in accordance with generally accepted 
auditing standards for any year used as a test year for ratemaking purposes. MPUC 
Rules, ch. 710, § 1; see also 35-A M.R.S. § 505(1). In support of its request, the District 
stated that it is unable to afford the cost of a full audit absent a rate increase, however, 
the District intends to initiate retroactive audits for the past several years and obtain 
financial audits going forward. As such, the District requests the Commission accept 
unaudited financial information in lieu of audited financial statements as support for its 
proposed rate increase pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 6014. 
III. 
DISCUSSION AND DECISION 
When requesting a waiver of Chapter 710, a petitioner must demonstrate there is 
good cause for granting that waiver and that granting a waiver would not be inconsistent 
with the purpose of the auditing requirement. MPUC Rules, ch. 710, § 5. When 
determining whether the petitioner has demonstrated good cause to waive a regulatory 
requirement, the Commission must consider the rule and applicable statutes. The 
purpose of the auditing requirement is to ensure a utility’s accounts are fairly and 
accurately represented and to detect any misstatements or errors in a utility’s books. 
However, in amending Chapter 710 to exempt small consumer owned water utilities 
from certain auditing requirements in 35-A M.R.S. § 505(1), the Legislature recognized 
the burden of accounting on small water utilities. See Maine Public Utilities Commission, 

1 The Commission has delegated the authority to issue a waiver from the requirements 
of Chapter 710 to the Director of Telephone and Water Utility Industries. MPUC Rules, 
ch. 710, § 5. 
Order Granting Waiver 
-2- 
Docket No. 2026-00178 
Amendments to Auditing Requirements for All Public Utilities (Chapter 710), Docket No. 
2011-00307, Order at 1 (Nov. 9, 2011). 
Considering the District’s financial position and intention to conduct retroactive 
audits, the Director of Telephone and Water Utility Industries finds good cause exists to 
waive the requirements of section 1 of Chapter 710 in this case. This waiver is limited to 
the instant rate increase proceeding. 
Accordingly, pursuant to Chapter 710, section 5, the Director of Telephone and 
Water Utility Industries grants a waiver of section 1 of Chapter 710 to allow the Monson 
Utilities District to file a request for a rate increase pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 6104 
without audited financial statements. 

Dated at Hallowell, Maine this Ninth Day of July, 2026 

BY ORDER OF THE DIRECTOR OF TELEPHONE AND WATER UTILITY 
INDUSTRIES 

/s/ Jody McColman 

Director of Telephone and Water Utility Industries 

Order Granting Waiver 
-3- 
Docket No. 2026-00178 
NOTICE OF RIGHTS TO REVIEW OR APPEAL 

5 M.R.S. § 9061 requires the Public Utilities Commission to give each party at 
the conclusion of an adjudicatory proceeding written notice of the party's rights to seek 
review of or to appeal the Commission's decision. The methods of review or appeal of 
Commission decisions at the conclusion of an adjudicatory proceeding are as follows: 

1. 
Reconsideration of the Commission's Order may be requested under Section 
11(D) of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (65-407 C.M.R. ch. 110) 
within 20 days of the date of the Order by filing a petition with the Commission stating 
the grounds upon which reconsideration is sought. Any petition not granted within 20 
days from the date of filing is denied. 

2. 
Appeal of a final decision of the Commission may be taken to the Law Court by 
filing, within 21 days of the date of the Order, a Notice of Appeal with the Administrative 
Director of the Commission, pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 1320(1)-(4) and the Maine Rules 
of Appellate Procedure. 

3. 
Additional court review of constitutional issues or issues involving the justness or 
reasonableness of rates may be had by the filing of an appeal with the Law Court, 
pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 1320(5). 

Pursuant to 5 M.R.S. § 8058 and 35-A M.R.S. § 1320(6), review of Commission 
Rules is subject to the jurisdiction of the Superior Court. 

Note: The attachment of this Notice to a document does not indicate the Commission's 
view that the particular document may be subject to review or appeal. Similarly, 
the failure of the Commission to attach a copy of this Notice to a document does 
not indicate the Commission's view that the document is not subject to review or 
appeal.

title: 2026-00103 Georgia Mountian Certification Order (002).pdf
text:
STATE OF MAINE 
PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION 

Docket No. 2026-00103 

July 9, 2026 

GREENBACKER RENEWABLE ENERGY 
CORPORATION 
Request for Approval of Certification 
For RPS Eligibility (Georgia Mountain Community 
Wind Facility) 

ORDER GRANTING NEW 
RENEWABLE RESOURCE 
CERTIFICATION 

BARTLETT, Chairman; SCULLY and GILBERT, Commissioners 
I. 
SUMMARY 
On April 14, 2026, Greenbacker Renewable Energy Company (Greenbacker 
Renewable), requested certification of a 10 megawatt (MW) wind facility located in 
Milton, VT (Georgia Mountain Community Wind Facility) as a Class I and Class IA 
renewable resource eligible to satisfy Maine’s new renewable resource portfolio (or 
renewable portfolio standard (RPS)) requirement pursuant to Chapter 311 of the 
Commission’s rules. For the reasons set forth below, the petition is granted. 
I. 
BACKGROUND 
A. 
New Renewable Resource Portfolio Requirement 
During its 2007 session, the Legislature enacted an Act To Stimulate Demand for 
Renewable Energy (2007 Act). P.L. 2007, ch. 403 (codified at 35-A M.R.S.A. section 
3210(3-A)). The 2007 Act added a mandate that specified percentages of electricity that 
supply Maine’s consumers come from “new” renewable resources.1 The 2007 Act 
defined a “new” renewable resource as renewable facilities that have an in-service date, 
resumed operation, or were refurbished after September 1, 2005. The percentage 
requirement started at one percent in 2008 and increased in annual 1% increments until 
it reached 10% by 2017. 
On June 26, 2019, the Governor signed L.D. 1494, An Act To Reform Maine’s 
Renewable Portfolio Standard, P.L. 2019, ch. 477 (2019 Act). The 2019 Act made 
changes to eligibility, removed the provision that the 10% requirement for Class I end in 
2022, created a new Class IA renewable resource portfolio requirement and a new 

1 Maine’s electric restructuring law, which became effective in March 2000, 
contained a portfolio requirement that mandated that at least 30% of the electricity to 
supply retail customers in the State come from eligible resources, which are either 
renewable or efficient resources. 35-A M.R.S.A. § 3210(3). 

ORDER GRANTING… 2 Docket No. 2026-00103 
thermal renewable energy resource requirement.2 It also applies a 300% multiplier for 
the output of a generator fueled by municipal solid waste in conjunction with recycling in 
Class II. 
The Commission modified its portfolio requirement rule (Chapter 311) to 
implement the provisions of the 2019 Act. Maine Public Utilities Commission, 
Amendments to Portfolio Requirement Rule (Chapter 311), Docket No. 2019-
00177, Order Amending Rule and Statement of Factual and Policy Basis (Nov. 8, 
2019) and Maine Public Utilities Commission, Amendments to Portfolio 
Requirement Rule (Chapter 311), Docket No. 2020-00212, Order Adopting Rule 
and Statement of Factual and Policy Basis (Nov. 13, 2020). 
Chapter 311 defines a Class I resource as a new renewable capacity resource. 
A “renewable capacity resource” is defined as a source of electrical generation: 
1. 
Whose total power production capacity does not exceed 100 megawatts 
and relies on one or more of the following: 
a. 
Fuel cells; 
b. 
Tidal power; 
c. 
Geothermal installations; 
d. 
Hydroelectric generators that meet all state and federal fish 
passage requirements applicable to the generator; 
e. 
Biomass generators that are fueled by wood, wood waste or landfill 
gas; or 
f. 
Anaerobic digestion of by-products of waste from animals or 
agricultural crops, food or vegetative material, algae or organic 
refuse; or 
2. 
That relies on wind power installations or solar power installations. 
MPUC Rules, ch. 311, § 2(Y). 
For a renewable capacity resource to qualify as “new,” a resource must be 
qualified hydroelectric output or a renewable capacity resource that meets one of 
the following criteria: 

2 The thermal renewable energy resource requirement began in 2021. 

ORDER GRANTING… 3 Docket No. 2026-00103 
1. 
Has an in-service date after September 1, 2005; 
2. 
Was added to an existing facility after September 1, 2005; 
3. 
For at least 2 years was not operated or was not recognized by the New 
England independent system operator as a capacity resource and, after 
September 1, 2005, resumed operation or was recognized by the New 
England independent system operator as a capacity resource[…]; or 
4. 
Was refurbished after September 1, 2005 and received certification 
from the Commission: 
a. 
Before September 1, 2019, that it is operating beyond its 
previous useful life or is employing an alternate technology that 
significantly increases the efficiency of the generation process; 
or 
b. 
On or after September 1, 2019, that it is operating beyond its 
previous useful life as evidenced by a finding that the facility 
would be reasonably likely to cease operation if not for 
substantial capital investment made after September 1, 2018, 
except for capital investment required to meet state and federal 
fish passage standards. 
Id. at § 2(T). 
A Class IA resource is defined as a Class I resource other than a Class I 
resource that for at least two years was not operated or was not recognized by the New 
England independent system operator as a capacity resource and, after September 1, 
2005, resumed operation or was recognized by the New England independent system 
operator as a capacity resource. Id. at § 2(F). 
Chapter 311 establishes a certification process that requires generators to pre- 
certify facilities as a Class I and/or Class IA resources under the requirements of the 
rule and provides for a Commission determination of resource eligibility on a case-by-
case basis. 
Finally, the rule specifies that the Commission may revoke a certification if there 
is a material change in circumstances that renders the generation facility ineligible as 
Class I or Class IA resource. Id. at § 3(C)(1). 
B. 
Petition for Certification 
In its April 14, 2026 petition, Greenbacker Renewable requested that the Georgia 
Mountain Community Wind Facility be certified as a Class I and Class IA renewable 
resource. According to the petition, the facility is a 10 MW AC wind facility located at 
345 North Road, Milton, VT 05468. The New England Power Pool Generation 
Information System Identification Number (NEPOOL GIS ID) for the facility is 
ORDER GRANTING… 4 Docket No. 2026-00103 
MSS35555. The facility’s initial commercial operation date was December 31, 2012. 
Because the facility is not located in Maine, the petition does not provide information on 
whether the facility will be serving load behind the meter (BTM) or providing kilowatt-
hour (kWh) credits under Maine’s Net Energy Billing (NEB) Kilowatt-hour Credit 
Program. On April 15, 2026, Greenbacker Renewable provided information about the 
facility’s certification for RPS standards in Connecticut, Massachusetts, Vermont and 
Rhode Island. On May 7, 2026, Greenbacker Renewable filed an amendment to the 
petition which provided additional documentation of the facility’s certification as a 
Vermont Tier IV resource. 
II. 
DECISION 
The Commission has delegated to the Director of the Electric and Gas Utility 
Industries the authority to certify generation facilities as Class I and Class IA new 
renewable resources and thermal renewable resources. Commission Initiated 
Delegation of Authority to Certify Class I New Renewable Resources, Docket No. 2008-
00184, Delegation Order (April 23, 2008); Commission Initiated Delegation of Authority 
to Certify Class IA New Renewable Resources and Thermal Renewable Resources, 
Docket No. 2021-00099, Delegation Order (May 11, 2021). Based on the information 
provided by Greenbacker Renewable, I conclude that the Georgia Mountain Community 
Wind Facility satisfies the eligibility requirements as both a Class I and Class IA 
resource. The facility is fueled by wind energy and commenced commercial operations 
after September 1, 2005. 
Accordingly, the Georgia Mountain Community Wind Facility is hereby certified 
as both a Class I and Class IA renewable resource eligible to satisfy Maine’s new 
renewable resource portfolio requirement pursuant to Chapter 311 of the Commission’s 
rules. Greenbacker Renewable or the facility’s successive owners or operators shall 
provide timely notice to the Commission of any material change in the characteristics or 
operation of the facility from that described in the petition filed in this proceeding. 
Greenbacker Renewable should also provide a copy of this Order to the administrators 
of NEPOOL GIS and/or the North American Renewables Registry (NAR). 
To the extent the output of the Georgia Mountain Community Wind Facility is 
serving load BTM, or providing kWh credits to customers under Maine’s NEB Kilowatt-
Hour Credit Program, the facility owner must retain GIS certificates or otherwise obtain 
GIS/NAR certificates necessary to satisfy Maine’s RPS for that portion of the BTM load 
that is served by the facility or the load associated with NEB kWh credits. See Lincoln 
Paper and Tissue, LLC, Request for Certification for RPS Eligibility, Docket No. 2008-
00173, Order Granting New Renewable Resource Certification at 8 (Jan. 27, 2009). If 
the output of the facility is used BTM or associated with NEB kWh credits, the facility 
owner shall submit to the Commission an annual report by September 1st of each year 
that demonstrates compliance with this requirement or a statement attesting that no 
output is used BTM or associated with NEB kWh credits. 

ORDER GRANTING… 5 Docket No. 2026-00103 
Dated at Hallowell, Maine, this 9th day of July, 2026. 

BY ORDER OF THE DIRECTOR OF THE ELECTRIC AND GAS UTILITY INDUSTRIES 

Sally Zeh 
_______________________________ 
Sally Zeh 

ORDER GRANTING… 6 Docket No. 2026-00103

text:
STATE OF MAINE 
PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION 

Docket No. 2026-00043 

July 9, 2026 

CENTRAL MAINE POWER COMPANY 
Request for Approval of Distribution Rate 
Change Pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 307 

PROCEDURAL ORDER 
(Schedule Amendments) 

I. 
DEADLINE FOR INTERVENOR TESTIMONY/BENCH ANALYSIS 

In light of the technical difficulties involving the Commission’s Case Management 
System (CMS), the Presiding Officers hereby find good cause to extend the deadline for 
intervenor testimony. Intervenor testimony and the bench analysis shall be filed no later 
than July 20, 2026. 
II. 
CMPRU REQUEST TO ADJUST SCHEDULE 
On July 8, 2026, CMP Ratepayers United (CMPRU) filed a Motion for Adjustment 
of Case Schedule to Permit Presentation of Intervenor Case (Motion).1 In its Motion, 
CMPRU requests an opportunity propound additional written discovery on Central 
Maine Power Company (CMP or the Company); an extension of the deadline to file the 
testimony of its expert witness Mark Ellis; and that written discovery on Mr. Ellis’s 
testimony to occur later than otherwise afforded by the current case schedule. In 
support of its Motion, CMPRU cites delays in the issuance of the Commission’s decision 
on its Petition for Preliminary Determination of Eligibility for Intervenor Funding, which 
was deliberated on July 1, 2026. See Mot. at 3. 

The Presiding Officers deny CMPRU’s request for additional discovery on CMP’s 
initial rate filing, specifically CMP’s proposed return on equity and cost of capital. 
CMPRU had a full and fair opportunity to engage in discovery—through both data 
requests and at a technical conference. While the Presiding Officers recognize CMPRU 
elected not to participate earlier in the case because it was unclear at that time whether 
it would be granted intervenor funding, nothing precluded CMPRU from doing so. 
Furthermore, there has been extensive discovery on CMP’s proposed rate of return and 
cost of capital, in which the Company has responded with its workpapers and answered 
questions regarding its experts’ underlying assumptions. 2 Therefore, the Presiding 
Officers do not find good cause to allow CMPRU to propound additional discovery 
requests on CMP outside the deadline for data requests. 

1 The Officer of the Public Advocate filed a response in support of CMPRU’s Motion on 
July 9, 2026. 
2 In making is request for additional discovery, CMPRU did not state whether it had 
reviewed the data responses provided to date or the reviewed the technical conference 
transcripts to determine whether they materials it seeks in discovery may already be 
available in the case. 
Procedural Order 
2 
Docket No. 2026-00043 

Concerning its request to extend the deadline for the filing of testimony and 
discovery thereon, the Presiding Officers have, as noted in Section I, extended the 
deadline from July 14, 2026, to July 20, 2026, for all parties. Data requests on the 
intervenor testimony and bench analysis are scheduled for July 28, 2026, with 
responses due August 11, 2026. While the Presiding Officers do not find CMPRU’s 
requested deadline of August 14, 2026, for the filing of its testimony to be reasonable 
given the statutory deadline in this proceeding and the need to maintain the case 
schedule, the Presiding Officers nevertheless find good cause to provide a modest 
extension in recognition of Mr. Ellis’s stated scheduling issues. See Mot. at 3-4. 
Therefore, Mr. Ellis’s testimony is due no later than August 3, 2026. Also, CMPRU must 
file with Mr. Ellis’s testimony any and all workpapers3 related thereto. No written 
discovery will be taken on Mr. Ellis’s testimony prior to the technical conference, and he 
will be subject to examination on August 27, 2026, at which time the parties may ask 
oral data requests for documents not otherwise filed with Mr. Ellis’s testimony and 
workpapers. 

Dated at Hallowell, Maine, this 9th day of July 2026. 
BY ORDER OF THE PRESIDING OFFICERS

Nora Healy 

/s/ Amy K. Olfene 
Amy K. Olfene

STATE OF MAINE 
PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION 
KENNEBUNK LIGHT & POWER DISTRICT 
Request for Waiver of Timing of Notice and 
Docket No. 2026-00181 
July 8, 2026 
ORDER GRANTING WAIVER 
REQUEST 
Customers’ Exercise of Opt-Out Right 
BARTLETT, Chairman; SCULLY and GILBERT, Commissioners 
On July 2, 2026, Kennebunk Light & Power District (KLPD) filed a request for 
waiver of the timeframes set forth in subsection 10(I) of Chapter 301 of the 
Commission’s rules. Subsection 10(I) provides that a consumer-owned transmission 
and distribution utility must provide its customers with notification of a standard offer 
load aggregation at least 90 days but no greater than 120 days before the initiation of 
such load aggregation service. KLPD requests approval to provide customer notification 
on or about July 28, 2026, which is approximately 156 days prior to the potential 
initiation of the standard offer load aggregation service rather than the standard 90 to 
120-day period set forth subsection 10(I) of Chapter 301.
Earlier this year in Docket No. 2026-00067, KLPD requested and was granted 
approval of revisions to its Rate SO (Standard Offer) rate schedule, as well as waivers 
of the timeframes provided in subsections 10(E) and 10(I) of Chapter 301.Kennebunk 
Light & Power District, Request for Approval of Tariff Revision and Waiver, Docket No. 
2026-00067, Order (Apr. 22, 2026). In that proceeding, KLPD sought to modify the 
timeframe by which KLPD must notify customers of its intent to offer standard offer load 
aggregation service and the timeframe by which customers must notify KLPD of their 
decision to opt-out from the load aggregation service. In its initial filing in that 
proceeding, KLPD requested a waiver of subsection 10(I) of Chapter 301 in order notify 
customers of its proposed standard offer load aggregation as soon as practicable. In its 
Order in Docket No. 2026-00067, the Commission noted that through the granting of the 
requested waivers, KLPD would be allowed to notify customers of the standard offer 
load aggregation sooner than 120 before the initiation of service. Id. at 3. 
Given this background, it is not clear that any additional waivers of Chapter 301 
are necessary in order for KLPD to provide customer notification in the timeframe 
described in its initial filing in this proceeding. The timeframe proposed by KLPD is 
consistent with the waivers previously granted in Docket No. 2026-00067. However, to 
the extent that additional Commission action is required in order to allow KLPD to 
proceed within its proposed timeframe, I find that good cause exists for the granting of 
Order Granting Waiver Request 
- 2 -
Docket No. 2026-00181 
any such waiver, as KLPD has indicated that doing so would allow it to secure the best 
supply opportunity for its customers.1 
Therefore, to the extent necessary and pursuant to the authority granted by 
section 11 of Chapter 301 of the Commission’s rules, I grant KLPD’s requested waiver 
of subsection 10(I) of Chapter 301. 
BY ORDER OF THE DIRECTOR OF ELECTRICITY AND GAS UTILITY INDUSTRIES 
Sally Zeh 
_______________________________ 
Sally Zeh 
1 In its Order in Docket No. 2026-00067, the Commission similarly found that there was 
good cause for waiving the Chapter 301 customer notice timing requirements because 
doing so would allow KLPD to more likely lock in favorable pricing that would benefit all 
KLPD customers.

NOTICE OF RIGHTS TO REVIEW OR APPEAL 

5 M.R.S. § 9061 requires the Public Utilities Commission to give each party at 
the conclusion of an adjudicatory proceeding written notice of the party's rights to seek 
review of or to appeal the Commission's decision. The methods of review or appeal of 
Commission decisions at the conclusion of an adjudicatory proceeding are as follows: 

1. 
Reconsideration of the Commission's Order may be requested under Section 
11(D) of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (65-407 C.M.R. ch. 
110) within 20 days of the date of the Order by filing a petition with the 
Commission stating the grounds upon which reconsideration is sought. Any 
petition not granted within 20 days from the date of filing is denied. 

2. 
Appeal of a final decision of the Commission may be taken to the Law Court by 
filing, within 21 days of the date of the Order, a Notice of Appeal with the 
Administrative Director of the Commission, pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 1320(1)-
(4) and the Maine Rules of Appellate Procedure. 

3. 
Additional court review of constitutional issues or issues involving the justness or 
reasonableness of rates may be had by the filing of an appeal with the Law 
Court, pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 1320(5). 

Pursuant to 5 M.R.S. § 8058 and 35-A M.R.S. § 1320(6), review of Commission 
Rules is subject to the jurisdiction of the Superior Court. 

Note: The attachment of this Notice to a document does not indicate the Commission's

title: 2026-07-08 PO 2026-00117 1.pdf
text:
STATE OF MAINE 
PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION 

Docket No. 2026-00091 

July 8, 2026 

GRAY WATER DISTRICT 
Request for Approval of Rate Change – 
6104 

PROCEDURAL ORDER 

I. 
BACKGROUND 
On April 28, 2026, the Gray Water District (the District) filed information 
supporting a proposed rate increase pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 6104 (section 6104) 
with the Commission. The initial filing comprised of rate increase documents, a copy of 
the customer notice, and proposed rate schedules. The District proposed an effective 
date of July 1, 2026, for the new rates. 
The District posted legal notice of the proposed rate increase and public witness 
hearing in the Portland Press Herald, on May 12, 2026. The District also mailed notice 
of the proposed rate change to its customers on March 1, 2026. 
On June 1, 2026, the District held a public hearing on the proposed rate 
increase, and informed customers at the public hearing of their right to petition the 
Commission and request a formal investigation. 
On June 11, 2026, the District made its final filing with the Commission. 
II. 
LEGAL STANDARD 
To implement a change of rates pursuant to the streamlined ratemaking process 
in 35-A M.R.S. § 6104, a consumer-owned water utility must comply with all of the 
requirements of that section. Subsection 6104(2) requires consumer-owned water 
utilities to hold “a public hearing at which the Public Advocate and any customer may 
testify and may question the officials present regarding the proposed rate change.” 
Subsection 6104(3) requires that consumer-owned water utility “provide notice of 
the proposed rate change and the date, time, place and purpose of the hearing to its 
customers.” The notice “must include a statement describing the amount of the rate 
change and the percentage change for each customer class, the customer’s right to 
request information relating to the present and proposed rates, the right to an open and 
fair hearing, and the right to further hearings before the commission, and the availability 
of assistance from the Public Advocate.” Subsection 6104(3) also requires the notices 
provided by consumer-owned water utilities to “inform customers that they can petition 
the [C]ommission to investigate the proposed rate change.” A utility may provide notice 
Procedural Order 
-2- 
Docket No. 2026-00117 
to customers by mailing notice to each customer and posting legal notice in a local 
newspaper or by following Chapter 616 of the Commission’s Rules.1 
Subsection 6104(4) requires that the consumer-owned water utility, at the public 
hearing, “inform those present [at the hearing] that the rate change may be investigated 
by the [C]ommission . . . and that petitions [for investigation] must bear the signatures 
and the printed names and the addresses of the signers.” 
Subsection 6104(4-A) requires that consumer-owned water utilities “file a copy of 
all materials supporting the proposed rate change with the [C]ommission and the Public 
Advocate, at least 30 days prior to the hearing” and that copies “of all material 
supporting the proposed rate change shall be made available to customers for 
examination at the offices of the utility for at least 30 days prior to the hearing.” 
Subsection 6104(5) requires consumer-owned water utilities to file their “changed 
rates with the [C]ommission within 30 days of the public hearing, but not sooner than 10 
days following the public hearing.” 
Subsection 6104(6) provides that the effective date of a proposed rate change 
must be at least one month, but not more than nine months, after the consumer-owned 
water utility files its final changed rates with the Commission. 
Subsection 6104(7) provides for suspension of the rate changes and 
Commission investigation of the change “[i]f, within 30 days of the public hearing, 15% 
of the customers of the consumer-owned water utility or 1,000 customers, whichever is 
less, file with the treasurer of the utility and with the [C]ommission petitions demanding 
a review of the rate changes.” 
Pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 310, the Commission “may at any time before the 
effective date of the [rate] change, either upon complaint or upon its own motion and 
after reasonable notice, hold a public hearing and make investigation as to the propriety 
of the proposed change.” 
III. 
PROCEDURAL ORDER 
Based upon the information in the Docket, the District satisfied all of the 
requirements of section 6104 except the provision requiring at least one month between 
the date of the District’s final filing of its changed rates and the effective date of those 
rates. See 35-A M.R.S. § 6104(6). Had the District proposed a later effective date 
thereby allowing it sufficient time to file its rates at least 30 days prior to the effective 

1 Chapter 616 provides that consumer-owned water utilities may be exempted from 
providing newspaper notice “provided that a utility provides notice of the public hearing 
by regular mail to all customers in addition to utilizing at least two of the following 
notification methods at least 14 days prior to the public hearing:” email, conspicuous 
posting in a town office or other conspicuous place, website, social media, or any other 
method “reasonably calculated to provide broad notice to the utility’s customers.” MPUC 
Rules, ch. 616, § 3(A). 
Procedural Order 
-3- 
Docket No. 2026-00117 
date, the District would have successfully complied with all of the requirements of 
section 6104. 
Because the District did not comply with all the provisions of Section 6104, the 
District’s rates did not go into effect on July 1, 2026, and may only go into effect upon 
approval by the Commission pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 307. 
Commission Staff intend to put the District’s proposed changed rates before the 
Commission for deliberation and approval at the earliest opportunity. 

Dated at Hallowell, Maine, this Eighth Day of July, 2026 

/s/ Jody McColman 

Director of Telephone and Water Utility Industries

title: 2026-00180 SNG COG_ProtectiveOrd No1 - Gas Supplier and Limited Cost of Gas Information (July 7 2026).pdf
text:
STATE OF MAINE 
PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION 
Docket No. 2026-00180 

July 7, 2026 
SUMMIT NATURAL GAS OF MAINE, INC., 
Request for Approval of Annual Cost of Gas 
Rate Adjustment (2026) 
PROTECTIVE ORDER NO. 1 
(Gas Supplier and Limited 
Cost of Gas Information) 

On July 1, 2026, Summit Natural Gas of Maine, Inc. (Summit or the Company) 
requested the issuance of Protective Order No. 1 (Gas Supplier and Limited Cost of 
Gas Information) to protect the confidentiality of commercially sensitive and proprietary 
information that Summit anticipates filing in this docket. 

In support of its motion, Summit states that it’s 2026 request for approval of a 
cost of gas rate adjustment will include proprietary information, such as projections of 
monthly throughput volumes for customer classes, estimates of gas supply costs and 
revenues, customer-specific information or any information from which customer 
information may be derived, and information concerning gas supply contracts or 
negotiations (collectively, the Cost of Gas Information). 

Summit states that the Commission has, in the recent past, issued protective 
orders protecting the confidentiality of similarly sensitive cost-of-gas information, 
including costs and charges related to the Atlantic Bridge Project (ABP) agreements. 
See, e.g., Summit Natural Gas of Maine, Inc., Request for Approval of Annual Cost of 
Gas Rate Adjustment (2025), Docket No. 2025-00213, Protective Order No. 1 (Gas 
Supplier Contract and Limited Cost of Gas Information) (July 10, 2025), Summit 
Natural Gas of Maine, Inc. Request for Approval of Annual Cost of Gas Information 
(2024), Docket No. 2024-00172 (Cost of Gas Information) (July 10, 2024), Summit 
Natural Gas of Maine, Inc. Request for Approval of Annual Cost of Gas Information 
(2023), Docket No 2023-00168, Protective Order No. 1 (Gas Supplier, Customer-
Specific Information, and Limited Cost of Gas Information) (July 12, 2023), Summit 
Natural Gas of Maine, Inc. Request for Approval of Annual Cost of Gas Adjustment 
(2022), Docket No. 2022-00214.Accordingly, Summit requests confidential treatment 
of the Cost of Gas Information in this proceeding. 

Summit further seeks a narrow scope of disclosure of the Cost of Gas 
Information and requests that access to such information be limited to the 
Commission, the Office of the Public Advocate, and their respective staff, consultants, 
and attorneys, and independent consultants to other parties in this proceeding. Summit 
notes that in the previous orders cited above, the Commission approved similarly 
narrow scopes of disclosures for local gas distribution companies where competitive 
disadvantage could result. 

Based on the foregoing, the Presiding Officers conclude that the limited and 
revocable protection requested by Summit is warranted under Rule 26(c) of the Maine 
Rules of Civil Procedure is warranted, subject to the requirements of 35-A M.R.S. § 
Protective Order No. 1 
2 Docket No. 2026-00180 

1311- A. Therefore, pursuant to Chapter 35-A M.R.S. § 1311-A, the Presiding Officers 
grant this Protective Order for the information regarding the substance of confidential 
agreements entered into by Summit. 

Any party at any time can move for a finding that material subject to protection 
should no longer be protected or that the other party should be provided access to the 
protected information pursuant to protective provisions. Unless such a motion is 
granted, however, use of the allegedly confidential materials continues to be restricted 
by the terms of this Protective Order. 

Accordingly, it is 

O R D E R E D 

1. 
That information that Summit designates as proprietary Cost of Gas 
Information, including information related to gas supplier arrangements, including costs 
and charges incurred from service under the Atlantic Bridge agreements as well as the 
confidential terms of such agreements themselves, customer-specific information, and 
competitively sensitive cost of gas information, shall constitute confidential information 
and such information shall be considered “Designated Confidential Information” for 
purposes of this Order. 

2. 
That all Designated Confidential Information shall, unless removed from 
the coverage of the Order as provided in Paragraph 3 below, be and remain 
confidential. Such Designated Confidential Information shall neither be used nor 
disclosed for any purpose other than the purposes of preparation and conduct of these 
proceedings, and then solely in accordance with this Order. No person to whom 
access to Designated Confidential Information is accorded pursuant to Paragraph 4 of 
this Order shall disclose or reveal, directly or indirectly, the content of the Designated 
Confidential Information to others except as provided in Paragraph 4. 

3. 
That the parties to whom such Designated Confidential Information is 
furnished may challenge the designation of such documents or other information as 
confidential by motion to the Commission and upon reasonable prior notice to the 
parties and an opportunity for hearing. In considering such a motion, the usual burdens 
of proof and production shall apply, and no additional presumption shall be given as a 
result of the prior designation of material as Confidential Information. Upon the entry to 
an order granting such a motion, the provisions and restrictions of this Order shall 
cease to bind any party or other person with respect to such documents or information 
as the Order granting the motion shall expressly and clearly remove from the coverage 
of this Order. 

4. 
That, unless the Order is modified, access to Designated Confidential 
Information shall be limited to (i) Commission members, members of the Commission 
Staff assigned to this proceeding and their consultants, (ii) the Public Advocate, 
members of the Public Advocate’s staff assigned to this proceeding and its consultants 
Protective Order No. 1 
3 Docket No. 2026-00180 

and counsel, (iii) a stenographer or reporter recording any hearing in connection with 
this proceeding, (iv) counsel for or any other representative of Summit, and (v) counsel 
and independent consultants for any party to this proceeding, provided that such 
Commission members, Commission staff, Public Advocate, Public Advocate staff, 
counsel, and consultants shall agree to use the Designated Confidential Information 
solely for purposes of this proceeding and not disclose the information to any other 
person and, provided further, that no counsel has “a personal and substantial financial 
interest that could be benefited by access to the information to the detriment of the 
party that provided the information.” 35-A M.R.S. §1311-A(1)(D)(2). In the event of 
additional intervenors in this case, this order may be modified in accordance with 35-A 
M.R.S. §1311-A after notice and opportunity to be heard. 

5. 
That all materials claimed by Summit to be Designated Confidential 
Information under the terms of this Order shall be clearly marked “confidential” by 
Summit. In the case of documents, each page of any document shall be stamped 
“confidential” in bold lettering in the upper right-hand corner of each page, including the 
cover letter. Any document or portion thereof not clearly and conspicuously marked 
“confidential” in bold lettering shall not be protected under the terms of this Order. 
Faxed materials should be marked as any other document. With regard to other media, 
diskettes should be marked “confidential” on the outside and, to the extent possible, 
each file on the diskette should be similarly identified. Any person or party subject to the 
terms of this Order who receives unmarked documents or materials which he/she 
believes Summit intended to be protected by the terms of this Order, and that would 
have been protected if marked in accordance with this paragraph, shall make a good 
faith effort to notify Summit of this fact and to avoid use of such documents or materials 
in a manner inconsistent with protection of such material under this Order. Summit shall 
also file a redacted public version of documents that contain Designated Confidential 
Information unless it seeks and obtains a waiver of this requirement from the presiding 
officer. Summit Gas shall also file redacted, public versions of documents that contain 
Designated Confidential Information unless it seeks and obtains a waiver of this 
requirement from the presiding officer. 

6. 
That the Confidential Settlement Information is not a “public record” 
pursuant to the Maine Freedom of Access Act (FOAA), 1 M.R.S. §§ 400-521, because 
the Presiding Officers have designated the Confidential Settlement Information as 
confidential pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. § 1311-A. 1 M.R.S. § 402(3)(A). 

7. 
That no copies of Designated Confidential Information shall be circulated 
to persons other than those persons who are authorized under Paragraph 4 of this 
Order to obtain Designated Confidential Information. Documents offered in evidence 
may be copied as necessary for that purpose. Persons authorized under Paragraph 4 
also may take such notes with regard to the Designated Confidential Information as 
may be necessary solely for the purposes of these proceedings. Such notes shall also 
be treated as Designated Confidential Information and shall not be used for any 
purposes other than the preparation and conduct of these proceedings. 

Protective Order No. 1 
4 Docket No. 2026-00180 

8. 
That the restrictions upon, and obligations accruing to, persons who 
become subject to this Order shall not apply to any Designated Confidential 
Information if the Commission rules, after reasonable notice and hearing, that such 
Designated Confidential Information was publicly known at the time it was furnished or 
has since become publicly known through no fault of the receiving party. 

9. 
That where any party wishes to introduce any Designated Confidential 
Information into the record, it shall give Summit sufficient notice so that Summit can 
move that any reference to Designated Confidential Information be made in camera, 
attended only by persons authorized to have access to such information under 
Paragraph 4, above. Where reference to Designated Confidential Information is 
required in pleadings, briefs, other legal documents, or argument, such reference shall 
be by citation of title or exhibit number only or by some other non-confidential 
description. In such circumstances, counsel shall preserve the confidentiality of 
material in the sealed record. If counsel shall include Designated Confidential 
Information in pleadings, briefs, other legal documents, or arguments, that portion of 
such documents or that portion of the transcript of such argument containing 
Designated Confidential Information shall be maintained under seal. 

10. 
This Order does not preclude any party from (a) objecting under the Maine 
Rules of Evidence to the admissibility of any Designated Confidential Information or (b) 
objecting, on any substantive or procedural ground, to any subsequent data request or 
other request for information. 

11. 
That a Party providing Designated Confidential Information may provide to 
each person having access to Designated Confidential Information a copy of this Order 
and require each person to agree in writing to the terms hereof prior to obtaining 
access to the Designated Confidential Information. 

12. 
That any Designated Confidential Information made part of the record in 
any proceeding before the Commission, including portions of the transcript of any 
hearing containing the content of the Designated Confidential Information, shall remain 
in the possession of the Commission, under seal, and subject to the protective 
requirements of this Order, unless the Commission or its authorized presiding officer 
shall otherwise order. 

13. 
That the Commission may draw upon all Designated Confidential 
Information in the record in the deliberation of any decision or order that it may issue, 
but the Commission will avoid public disclosure or the reproduction in its decision of 
any Designated Confidential Information. 

14. 
That should any appeal of or other challenge to the Commission’s decision in this 
proceeding be taken, any portions of the record that have been sealed in accordance 
with Paragraph 8 above shall be forwarded to the courts of this State in accordance with 
applicable law and procedures, but under seal and so designated in writing for the 
information of the court. 
Protective Order No. 1 
5 Docket No. 2026-00180 

15. 
That this Order may be modified on motion of any party or on the 
Commission’s own motion upon reasonable prior notice to the parties and an 
opportunity for hearing. 

16. 
That Copies of Designated Confidential Information and documents, 
notes, and other materials containing or reflecting, directly or indirectly, the Designated 
Confidential Information, that are in the possession of members, counsel or staff of the 
Commission or of the Office of the Public Advocate may be retained by those persons 
for the purpose of performing those persons’ duties and obligations. If retained, the 
Designated Confidential Information shall be subject to this Protective Order or to a 
protective order issued in another proceeding in which the Designated Confidential 
Information is used. If a member, counsel or staff of the Commission or the Office of 
the Public Advocate does not retain the Designated Confidential Information, that 
person shall destroy it as provided in this paragraph. Within forty (40) days after the 
Commission reaches a final decision (i.e., unappealable) in this proceeding, each other 
party and independent consultants and experts retained by the Commission or the 
Office of the Public Advocate to whom Designated Confidential Information has been 
made available shall return to Summit Designated Confidential Information and shall 
destroy all documents, notes and other materials containing or reflecting, directly or 
indirectly, Designated Confidential Information; provided, however, that the sealed 
record shall be retained by the Commission and shall continue to remain subject to the 
confidentiality requirements of this Order, until otherwise ordered by the Commission. 
Audio, video or other such magnetically recorded materials shall be electronically 
erased before disposal. Documents shall be shredded. 

Dated at Hallowell, Maine, this 7th day of July 2026 
BY ORDER OF THE PRESIDING OFFICERS 
Carol A. MacLennan 

Vanessa H. Bean
